In [[differential geometry]], '''Huisken's monotonicity formula''' states that, if an {{mvar|n}}-dimensional surface in {{math|(''n'' + 1)}}-dimensional [[Euclidean space]] undergoes the [[mean curvature flow]], then its [[convolution]] with an appropriately scaled and time-reversed [[heat kernel]] is non-increasing.<ref name="m">{{citation
 | last = Mantegazza | first = Carlo
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-0348-0145-4
 | isbn = 978-3-0348-0144-7
 | mr = 2815949
 | contribution = 3.1 The Monotonicity Formula for Mean Curvature Flow
 | pages = 49–52
 | publisher = Birkhäuser/Springer | location = Basel
 | series = Progress in Mathematics
 | title = Lecture notes on mean curvature flow
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=l2muz9qOAosC&pg=PA51
 | volume = 290
 | year = 2011}}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = Bellettini | first = Giovanni
 | contribution = 4 Huisken's monotonicity formula
 | doi = 10.1007/978-88-7642-429-8
 | isbn = 978-88-7642-428-1
 | mr = 3155251
 | pages = 59–68
 | publisher = Edizioni della Normale | location = Pisa
 | series = Appunti. Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa (Nuova Serie) [Lecture Notes. Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa (New Series)]
 | title = Lecture notes on mean curvature flow, barriers and singular perturbations
 | volume = 12
 | year = 2013}}.</ref> The result is named after [[Gerhard Huisken]], who published it in 1990.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Huisken | first = Gerhard | author-link = Gerhard Huisken
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Journal of Differential Geometry
 | mr = 1030675
 | pages = 285–299
 | title = Asymptotic behavior for singularities of the mean curvature flow
 | url = http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.jdg/1214444099
 | volume = 31
 | year = 1990| doi = 10.4310/jdg/1214444099 | doi-access = free
 | hdl = 11858/00-001M-0000-0013-5CFE-3
 | hdl-access = free
 }}.</ref>

Specifically, the {{math|(''n'' + 1)}}-dimensional time-reversed heat kernel converging to a point {{math|''x''<sub>0</sub>}} at time {{math|''t''<sub>0</sub>}} may be given by the formula<ref name="m"/>
:<math>u(x,t) = \frac{1}{(4\pi (t_0-t))^{n/2}}\exp\left(-\frac{|x-x_0|^2}{4(t_0-t)}\right).</math>
Then Huisken's monotonicity formula gives an explicit expression for the [[derivative]]
of
:<math>\int u(x,t) d\mu,</math>
where {{mvar|&mu;}} is the area element of the evolving surface at time {{mvar|t}}. The expression involves the negation of another integral, whose integrand is non-negative, so the derivative is non-positive.

Typically, {{math|''x''<sub>0</sub>}} and {{math|''t''<sub>0</sub>}} are chosen as the time and position of a singularity of the evolving surface, and the monotonicity formula can be used to analyze the behavior of the surface as it evolves towards this singularity. In particular, the only surfaces for which the convolution with the heat kernel remains constant rather than decreasing are ones that stay self-similar as they evolve, and the monotonicity formula can be used to classify these surfaces.

[[Grigori Perelman]] derived analogous formulas for the [[Ricci flow]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Perelman | first = Grigori | author-link = Grigori Perelman
 | arxiv = math/0211159
 | title = The entropy formula for the Ricci flow and its geometric applications
 | year = 2002| bibcode = 2002math.....11159P}}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Cao | first1 = Huai-Dong
 | last2 = Hamilton | first2 = Richard S. |author-link=Huai-Dong Cao|author-link2=Richard S. Hamilton
 | last3 = Ilmanen | first3 = Tom
 | arxiv = math/0404165
 | quotation = There are also two monotonicity formulas of shrinking or localizing type ... Either of these can be seen as the analogue of Huisken's monotonicity formula for mean curvature flow.
 | title = Gaussian densities and stability for some Ricci solitons
 | year = 2004| bibcode = 2004math......4165C}}.</ref>
